scenes.title: Verify the shift occurrence and approval rule
scenes.narration_exact: Open the intended day in Responder's Shifts workspace. Here, Community standby signup is scheduled for Sunday, November first, from eight until noon. You are on confirms this account's current roster membership. Read the notice that sign-ups and trades need supervisor approval before changing coverage. Request trade is available for this occurrence. Verify the day and time first, especially when the same shift name appears on several dates.

scenes.title: Read the request form and candidate identities
scenes.narration_exact: Choose Request trade to open Request a trade. The explanation says that everyone you pick is asked, and then you choose from their offers. Read the candidate names with their groups and roles. Blake Gallo is shown with Truck eighty-one and Firefighter. The other displayed candidates remain separate choices. This is where you decide whom you intend to ask; a displayed name is not an accepted offer or an approved replacement.

scenes.title: Select one person and review the note
scenes.narration_exact: Select the checkbox for the intended person. This exercise selects only Blake Gallo, and Selected, one confirms the count. Enter a clear Note explaining the request. scenes.title: Check the saved request notice
scenes.narration_exact: Choose Send request once. The returned day detail says, You have asked colleagues to take this shift, and offers Cancel trade request. You are on remains visible, along with the supervisor-approval rule. These details establish the saved request state shown here. They do not show an accepted offer, supervisor approval or a completed handover. Keep your department's actual coverage arrangements clear while the request is outstanding.

scenes.title: Read the outgoing entry and response state
scenes.narration_exact: Close the day sheet and choose Trades. Under In progress, find the standby entry with the intended date and time. It is marked Outgoing and Open, and includes the saved training Note. Responses lists Blake Gallo with No reply yet. Read the actual response label before planning a replacement. In this recorded exercise, the colleague has not replied, and the request has not produced an accepted coverage agreement.

scenes.title: Review and confirm cancellation
scenes.narration_exact: Choose Cancel trade request on that outgoing entry. The confirmation asks, Cancel this trade request, and repeats the shift name, date and time. Read the warning that any offers you have received will be discarded. This example's preceding response state was No reply yet. Verify the identity in the confirmation, then choose the red Cancel trade request button to carry out the intended cancellation.

Read the application's actual returned state when doing this in your department; this view does not present a separate cancellation-history record.

scenes.title: Return to the matching Calendar card
scenes.narration_exact: Choose Calendar to return to the day cards. Find Sunday, November first, and compare the Community standby signup card with the cancelled request. Its eight-to-noon time range, You are on label and Approval required label remain visible. Open this matching card to recheck the saved day detail. Using the full date and hours keeps a familiar shift name from being confused with a different occurrence.

scenes.title: Use clear request states in any department
scenes.narration_exact: Use the same identity and result checks when community paramedicine or mental health teams request outreach coverage, search-and-rescue teams arrange support, security companies cover a post, wildland contractors coordinate a crew, or industrial response teams plan standby staffing. Fire and EMS departments can apply them to station coverage. Keep a request, a colleague's response, required approval and the final roster assignment distinct, and verify the actual result of each operation your department performs.
